title: Artificial (harp) harmonics
description: A harp-harmonic figure, as Tommy Emmanuel's arrangements use it: the left hand holds a shape (D string at 7, G string at 9) and the right hand touches each string an octave above the fret held and plucks it, alternating with ordinary notes on the B and E strings. MNX pitch is sounding, so each harmonic stores what is heard (A4, E5), the stopped fret is stored on the note, and harmonic.touchingPitch names the node; the derivation ladder works out the fret held from the node rather than from the sounding pitch. Tab prints the TOUCH fret in a diamond, as published tab does (◇19, ◇21) — the held fret is implied an octave below — and prints the held fret before the diamond when the node is not the octave: the seventh event is held at 2 on the G string and touched at 9, a twelfth up, drawn 2◇9. Notation gives each harmonic a diamond notehead at the sounding pitch with its label (A.H.); the natural harmonic's circle is not used. The plain notes are drawn as ever.
